correctness.rationale: Since 0<t_m<1, the origin is interior to every disk. Along each radial direction the farthest center is the one nearest the opposite direction, so the active circle changes at the bisectors, producing exactly m genuine arcs. At a switching point of radial distance s, resolving the unit vector from the center gives sin β=s sin α and cos β=t_m+s cos α, hence sin(α−β)=t_m sin α and β=(π−u)/m. Polygon area plus the m unit circular segments gives A_m=mβ−m sin β sin(α−β)/sin α, including the zero polygon area of the lens. For F(x)=sin(ux)sin((π−u)x)/(x sin πx), the sign of its logarithmic derivative after multiplication by x is g(ux)+g((π−u)x)−g(0)−g(πx), where g(z)=z cot z. Strict concavity on [0,π/2] makes this positive by applying the strict chord inequality twice. This yields strict increase of A_m and the disk limit from F(0)=u(π−u)/π. Taylor expansion gives the deficit coefficient u²(π−u)²/(3π). With q=P/2 the formula is q−(m/2)sin(2q/m)+m cot(π/m)sin²(q/m), giving both small-perimeter expansions and the zero quadratic term at m=2. Expanding instead at u=0 gives A_m=π−2u+cot(π/m)u²/m+O_m(u³). The frozen numerical script was inspected, not executed; none of the strict claims depends on sampled inequalities.
residual_risks: Only planar unit disks in the specified regular orbits and strict interior perimeters; no optimum over irregular configurations is inferred.
